approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and walks through batches of fresh local graph edits, including direct formula-preserving exchanges of aromatic nitrogen and carbon positions. It sanitizes each graph, repairs its canonical identity before duplicate checks, and submits the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. A selected transition installs at most four signed local attributes for four completed steps, with overlapping attributes refreshed to the latest transition. The current veto needs only one positive and one negative inverse match from the same transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current state even after a worsening move; equal maxima use the canonical lexical order, and an independent archive retains the best observed molecule.
approach.novelty: Require a candidate to match every currently live inverse attribute belonging to one selected transition before that transition can veto it, while still requiring both inverse signs. This makes the veto respond to a complete retained signature instead of any two opposite-sign fragments. Earlier memory siblings changed single-attribute matching to a two-sign rule or withheld memory credit from nonimproving moves. This experiment keeps credit for every selected move and changes only how completely a candidate must match the stored signature; the neighborhood extensions already present in the Parent remain in place.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes all fifteen task sessions with macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population standard deviation 0.006329100643035156; its paired gain over the repaired predecessor is only 0.0008412882577690054. Its memory stores up to four inverse attributes of a selected transition but can veto after matching only one attribute of each sign. Independent read-only reconstruction of all saved Parent logs reproduces 195 vetoes among 4545 valid novel draws. Only 65 of those draws match every live attribute of any qualifying transition. The remaining 130 vetoed draws cover 99 batches and 123 distinct molecular identities counted within their task/seed sessions, with opportunities in all fifteen sessions: 66 match two of four live attributes, seven match two of three, and 57 match three of four. They include 47 add_path, 21 change_atom, 19 close_ring, 16 delete_leaf, 14 open_ring, seven insert_path, four contract_atom and two change_bond draws. For example, seed-0 deco_hop batch 3 attempt 33 adds a terminal carbon to the current CNCOC side chain and matches restriction ids 5 and 7 from transition 2 while leaving ids 6 and 8 unmatched; the Parent still vetoes it. These are measured incomplete-signature exclusions, with no score assigned to an excluded draw. The earlier bidirectional-memory node n-d88727c16484 established that partial motif matching can redirect many submissions but did not identify the value of the surviving vetoes. On the current Parent, n-a240f72e3717 withheld credit from nonimproving transitions and lost 0.020273360127168 in paired mean despite admitting 74 scored neighbors. That negative result motivates testing candidate-signature completeness while preserving credit for every selected transition, rather than assuming that all weaker memory rules are beneficial.
hypothesis: Veto a valid novel neighbor only when its signed motif changes match every currently live inverse restriction of at least one selected-transition provenance group and that complete group contains both inverse signs, replacing the Parent's one-match-per-sign criterion without changing memory credit or lifecycle.

finding_summary.headline: Complete-signature memory admitted 113 scored neighbors, but lowered every seed's macro score
finding_summary.insights: Incomplete motif matches do exclude some useful variations: newly admitted methyl addition, ring opening and aryl substitution produced real archive gains. A newly admitted phenol-oxygen deletion was selected despite a score loss, then a newly admitted hydroxymethyl addition in the next batch produced the strongest observed DRD2 molecule. Those concrete successes did not rescue the overall score claim. The checks rule out an unexercised predicate, missing feedback, loss of unconditional memory credit, altered expiry or restored historical signatures as explanations for the negative panel result. Requiring full motif coverage reduces exclusions as intended, but this panel shows that greater matching specificity is not sufficient to identify restrictions that can be removed beneficially. Whether the partial-signature vetoes help diversification remains open: once batch membership changes, later source graphs and random-stream consumption change, and ancestry alone cannot assign the final score difference to one admitted edit. The chemistry assessment also finds persistent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur environments, difficult ring geometry and absent stereochemical assignments alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families. The stronger individual molecules therefore do not establish improved chemical feasibility or broader useful scaffold coverage.
finding_summary.results: On the Child's actual source states and live memory tables, the inherited rule would veto 178 fresh draws; the complete-signature rule vetoed 65 and admitted the other 113. Every new admission was evaluated, affecting 96 batches across all fifteen task sessions, and twenty became next states. Fifteen improved on their source, five tied and 93 worsened it; five produced immediate archive gains. Complete signatures still vetoed 63 distinct fresh molecular identities, including a two-attribute group left after overlap replacement. Memory credit, four-step tenure and overlap handling were preserved. All budgets and batches completed, using 5209 generation attempts versus the Parent's 5303. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.482572, a paired change of -0.039187 against the required +0.002. All three seed means declined. Four task means fell; median_2 rose by 0.002696. The largest task-mean losses were sitagliptin (-0.104268) and DRD2 (-0.075446). Across all accepted proposals, source improvements fell from 468 to 436, and strict archive improvements changed from 238 to 237 while their total magnitude fell from 4.699005 to 4.111202.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl families, amine-bearing bridged cores and sulfur-heavy polycycles lack consistent stability and stereochemical control
molecular.overall_character: All five tasks and all supplied parent trajectories were read. Each task digest covers 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output is richly cyclic and usually aromatic: ring_closure_rate and branch_rate are 1.0 throughout; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.908, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.9437 in the supplied task order. These are molecule-level SMILES-text counters, not aromatic atom fractions or measures of feasible ring geometry. There are recognizable indole carboxanilides, nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, aryl-linked amines and cyclic amide/ketone systems, together with extensive reactive heteroatom attachments and densely connected sulfur-containing cages. The ordinary members make an across-the-board judgement of chemical impossibility inappropriate, but the recurrent liabilities justify questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall drug-likeness. Distinct identities and several scaffold families support moderate diversity; the upper excerpts nevertheless repeatedly reuse particular cores and vary their appendages. charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are both 0.0 for every task. Free amines and potentially stereogenic ring junctions are visibly present, so these zeros mean absent charge/configuration notation, not absent ionization or stereochemistry. Heavy-atom ranges below were counted directly with RDKit from every supplied optimizer trajectory; no property oracle or new molecule was evaluated. The parent has the same broad chemical families and liabilities. The comparisons below describe observed chemistry and recorded scores, without attributing changes to the algorithm mechanism. Missing-feature statements distinguish gaps in chemical coverage from a required pharmacophore, which these trajectories alone cannot establish. There are no tasks without trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer products contain 21–29 heavy atoms. All contain rings and most contain aromatic atoms, with ring_closure_rate 1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.908. The upper excerpt includes relatively ordinary ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilides and amino-substituted benzothiophene carbonyl derivatives. The seed-0 leader instead links an aminopyridine through a ketone to a bridged, partly aromatic thiophene-containing core bearing amino and hydroxymethyl groups. Later molecules retain similar size but accumulate partially reduced rings, extra closures, aminated carbon centres and halogenated side chains. The simple aromatic amides look more approachable synthetically than those multiply connected late polycycles.
liabilities: Cited upper members include free thiols, chloromethyl substituents and thioesters; later upper members also contain N–F bonds on heavily substituted side chains. These are chemical handling or stability concerns that the score does not resolve.
Late products combine small ring junctions with unsaturation and unassigned stereocentres. Ring-closure notation establishes connectivity, not a feasible conformation or synthesis.
missing_features: The useful compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is not consistently preserved in the later molecules. Coverage of conventional alternative heteroaryl carbonyl frameworks is limited relative to the many reductions and extra ring connections.

Defined configurations and tractable geometric alternatives for the bridged analogues are absent. The visible gradient does not identify an additional obligatory functional group that all these molecules lack.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue at seed 1, evaluation 61 scores 0.39905049777278273. The bridged aminopyridyl ketone at seed 0, evaluation 170 scores 0.40196779766986834. A modified indole whose carbonyl linker has become a substituted saturated carbon at seed 0, evaluation 42 scores 0.03343008011310944, and the N-chlorinated, partly reduced ring system at seed 1, evaluation 234 scores 0.010020601872687556. Together these observations favour preservation of a compact carbonyl-linked aromatic/heteroaromatic arrangement within the shown series; neither more rings nor more heteroatoms alone explains the scores. The parent has the identical seed-1 leader, while its seed-2 leader is an N-chloro benzofuran carboxanilide scoring 0.41003927643747895; this node instead retains a thiol-bearing indole carboxanilide as the seed-2 best at 0.3748218641899741. Thus the chemical comparison includes a more conventional amide at a lower recorded endpoint, rather than evidence that the objective reliably rewards synthetic plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest products by heavy-atom range, 30–49, with mean SMILES length 70.0 and ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate both 1.0. The leading excerpt repeatedly retains a fused nitrogen-containing dicarbonyl heterocycle with two pyridyl appendages, an amino linker, ethers and a dimethylaminomethyl ether side chain. The same structures also carry an oxygen–fluorine bond and an imide nitrogen–chlorine bond. Terminal chains vary between alkyl, alkenyl, alkynyl and cumulated-double-bond forms. Other seeds explore related heavily decorated aromatic heterocycles with sulfur-containing attachments. The initial and lower-scoring molecules already possess sizable aromatic ester/phenol/lactam frameworks; this is not a progression from fragments to ordinary drug-like scaffolds.
liabilities: O–F and N–Cl attachments are unusually reactive choices for an otherwise medicinal-looking heteroaromatic scaffold. Aminomethyl ethers add another potentially labile connection.

cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1839 across proposals. The cited carbon cumulenes and sulfur cumulene share the upper score with more conventional chains, so the visible objective does not separate their chemical plausibility.
Substantial appendage growth, flexible chains and unassigned centres complicate an already large scaffold; formal graph validity does not supply a practical route.
missing_features: The upper plateau lacks a systematic matched set of conventional alternatives to the oxygen–fluorine and nitrogen–chlorine connections while retaining the same aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. Their replacement cannot be assumed to preserve score without observation.

There is limited upper-excerpt coverage of distinct core frameworks that reproduce the polar attachment pattern. Tied tail variants do not identify a further required functional group or demonstrate broader scaffold coverage.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.548381482770623. A lower optimizer product with altered carbonyl/unsaturation around that core scores 0.5286081645773063. Every molecule in the best excerpt scores exactly 0.6118152178904348 despite changes to terminal chains, branching, an alkyne linker and even a sulfur-containing cumulene. The upper cluster therefore associates a retained carbonyl/heteroaryl framework and its decoration with higher scores, but provides no gradient selecting a particular terminal unsaturation or demonstrating the value of the reactive N–Cl/O–F attachments. The parent seed-2 best at 0.6092182584436399 is also a heavily decorated fused dicarbonyl system with different side chains. Its seed-0 best reaches 0.6161710037174721 in a larger sulfur-containing carbonyl/thiocarbonyl family. The chemistry has shifted among related decorated heterocycles, with persistent liabilities in both nodes.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer products span 28–43 heavy atoms. All have rings and aromatic atoms, and halogen_rate is 0.9966. The seed-1 upper family has a densely bridged aryl nitrogen framework, an enamine-like connector, a secondary amine-containing chain to a chlorophenyl group, an aryl amino group and phenol or hydroxymethyl substitution. Its leading members are sulfur-free. The wider output also contains many very different sulfur-bearing amine polycycles; the final seed-2 excerpt is dominated by densely connected, sulfur-rich cages. The low optimizer examples retain the initial biaryl carboxylic acid, amide and N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine pattern, whose conventional functional groups are synthetically more familiar than the later sulfur networks.
liabilities: The upper family combines substantial halogenated aromatic surface with enamine and aryl-amine functionality and unspecified bridge stereochemistry. These features merit chemical scrutiny even at high recorded score.

The final seed-2 examples include carbon–sulfur triple bonds, multiple hydrogen-bearing multivalent sulfur centres, sulfur–sulfur connectivity and densely overlapping rings. Their synthesis and stable three-dimensional realization are especially questionable.
missing_features: A controlled variety of conventional amine-bearing ring and linker arrangements at comparable aryl distances is not demonstrated in the leading family; its favourable free-amine presentation remains tied to a dense bridged framework. A particular named amine ring is not established as a missing requirement.

Assigned configurations and realistic conformational alternatives for the bridged cores are absent. charged_rate 0.0 does not mean the free amines cannot protonate, and the submitted strings do not reveal any protonation treatment used during scoring.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A near-initial acid/amide/sulfonamide analogue scores 0.007468397818197266, whereas the free-amine, hydroxymethyl-bearing bridged aryl leader scores 0.9492384404345239. This is consistent with preference for the displayed arrangement of aromatic surfaces and accessible non-acylated nitrogen, but many structural changes intervene. The linker secondary amine is not demonstrably obligatory: cited analogues without it still score 0.9214072921127627 and 0.9265115835486502. A carbon connector and its unusual sulfur replacement each score 0.9341451805829589. Relative to the parent, the seed-1 best changes from a sulfur-containing bridged aryl system at 0.868020189804352 to the sulfur-free leader, while the seed-2 best changes from a sulfur-containing amine polycycle at 0.9148143511682032 to a more sulfur-heavy cage at 0.630083597033273. The current chemistry therefore includes both a cleaner upper family and persistent problematic sulfur architectures; the scores do not establish a general benefit from sulfur removal.

per_task.generated_character: These products span 28–43 heavy atoms, with ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate both 1.0. The leading seed-2 family combines phenyl and propyl-substituted oxygen-bridged arene groups with a partially saturated nitrogen heterocycle fused to a larger ring containing a ketone, an N-methyl amide, another amine and a methoxy-bearing amino carbon. The leading member is sulfur-free; nearby members introduce a hydrogen-bearing multivalent sulfur centre or an N–S connection. Other seeds retain related aryl-substituted cyclic amide/amine families. These have recognizable medicinal-chemistry components but less routine medium-ring assembly and configuration requirements.
liabilities: Medium-ring closures and aminoether centres require conformational and stereochemical control that is not encoded in these strings.

Nearby high-scoring products contain unusual sulfur-hydride environments or N–S bonds. Lower members also retain O–Br groups and N–N connections; their presence is not evidence of a useful or stable pharmacophore.
missing_features: Coverage of conventional alternative cyclic frameworks retaining the apparent aryl/carbonyl spacing is limited. The best excerpt concentrates around one enlarged heterocycle and does not establish a specific additional missing pharmacophore.
Configuration-defined aminoether and ring-junction variants, together with route-consistent alternatives to the larger ring closures, are absent from the shown output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329, and the current seed-2 leader scores 0.20992737768880673. An opened carbonyl-containing side-chain analogue scores 0.12467972074136988. Late variants that contract the phenyl ring to a nonaromatic diene or remove a carbonyl score 0.1890295187081868 and 0.19855299930894993 respectively. The visible association is with cyclic presentation of the aryl and carbonyl groups, rather than aromaticity or molecular size alone. Sulfur is not required by the upper excerpt: the sulfur-free leader sits alongside related sulfur-bearing molecules at 0.2078390661284897 and 0.20641345956774915. The parent seed-2 best at 0.20185639717998205 is a larger aryl-substituted cyclic carbonyl/amine framework; the present seed-2 upper family retains that broad architecture with different ring connections and decoration. The parent seed-0 best at 0.21196904390980506 also belongs to an aryl/cyclic amide family, so the supplied chemistry does not demonstrate departure into unrelated high-scoring scaffolds.

per_task.generated_character: The products contain 26–37 heavy atoms but frequently pack them into dense fused and bridged sulfur-rich systems. ring_closure_rate is 1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9437 across proposals; nevertheless, the leading seed-2 molecule and its closely related ring-contracted analogue have no aromatic atoms in their parsed graphs. The leader has six sulfur atoms, an imine, an ester ring, a sulfur–oxygen double bond, N–S connections, carbon-bound fluorine and multiple unusual sulfur-hydride/double-bond environments. Other upper members retain carbonyl/imino nitrogen heterocycles, acyl fluoride or N-fluorinated groups within highly connected cages. These are compact by atom count, but their bonding and topology make their synthetic plausibility particularly poor.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing multivalent sulfur, carbon–sulfur multiple bonds, sulfur–sulfur single-bond connections, N–S attachments and dense ring intersections present substantial stability, geometry and synthesis concerns.

Cited upper members include acyl fluoride and N–F bonds as well as free sulfur-containing terminal groups. Formal parsing and high recorded scores do not establish that these are stable medicinal compounds.
No stereochemistry is assigned despite complex junctions and potentially stereogenic sulfur or carbon environments.
missing_features: A chemically conventional realization of the compact polar-atom and fluorine arrangement associated with the upper scores is not established; the current realization is dominated by unusual sulfur bonding.

Alternative frameworks with regular ring geometry and assigned configurations are absent from the leading excerpt. The supplied scores do not identify a required amine class or another particular absent functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.0020944534688323298, and an expanded carbonyl heterocycle at seed 2, evaluation 17 scores 7.590554525032884e-10. The sulfur-rich, partly imino leader at evaluation 284 scores 0.44981689162204463. Close late variants score 0.3717269599472881 after shortening a bridge, 0.2831350668795932 after removing the imine methyl, 0.0847360681405348 after inserting an amino-containing linker, and 0.40618640040890686 after contracting the ester-containing ring. The observable gradient is sensitive to the particular compact topology, substitution and polar-atom arrangement. Neither aromaticity nor simply adding sulfur explains it; other sulfur-rich structures in the low excerpt also have extremely small scores. The parent already produced similarly unusual sulfur-containing cages, with seed-0 and seed-1 best scores 0.48118636011729826 and 0.5903526424693334. The current upper chemistry preserves that problematic family rather than supplying a conventional structural interpretation of the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Upper-excerpt molecules include oxygen–fluorine and nitrogen–chlorine bonds, sulfur cumulenes, acyl fluoride, N–F groups and dense sulfur-hydride networks. A carbon connector and an unusual sulfur counterpart share the recorded score 0.9341451805829589; conventional tails and cumulene tails also share 0.6118152178904348. These observed ties show that chemical plausibility cannot be inferred from the available scalar score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks consistent control of reactive heteroatom attachments and unusual sulfur bonding.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need bond-context-aware alternatives that distinguish ordinary aromatic sulfur, thioethers and carbonyl chemistry from reactive heteroatom–halogen connections and unusual multivalent sulfur. Coherent replacements should preserve useful attachment patterns so their value can be measured through actual feedback; the evidence does not justify rejecting every sulfur-containing molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited leaders and late molecules include bridged polycycles, small ring intersections, aminoether centres and unusual sulfur junctions that can require configurations and constrained geometry. Thus missing ring formation is not the gap; the missing coverage is chemically coherent realizations of those connections.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring connectivity is abundant, but realistic geometry and explicit stereochemical coverage remain weak.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Introduce task-independent ring-topology and bond-geometry awareness, together with configuration-defined alternatives when the existing graph permits them. Preserve ordinary aromatic and polar motifs while exploring realizable closures. The effect of assigning configurations or restricting closures must be measured, since the current score records establish no stereochemical preference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Distinct molecules and several ring families are present, but the upper excerpts repeatedly retain the same fused dicarbonyl core, enlarged aryl-substituted carbonyl ring, bridged aryl amine core or sulfur-rich cage. The entire 0.6118152178904348 excerpt varies decorations on one framework, including chemically very different terminal unsaturation. This supports moderate output diversity without demonstrating broad coverage of chemically distinct upper-score scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring structural variety is concentrated in reused scaffold families with changing appendages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need coherent replacements of ring frameworks and linkers that preserve generic aryl, donor and acceptor attachment relationships while changing the underlying scaffold. Evaluate those alternatives with task-local feedback, without naming a desired target or reference compound. Merely creating another canonical identity is insufficient evidence of new chemical coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An upper-excerpt molecule with a free secondary amine, aryl amino group and hydroxymethyl substituent scores 0.9492384404345239, while a shown acid/amide/sulfonamide structure scores 0.007468397818197266. Many other features differ, and analogues without the linker secondary amine still score 0.9214072921127627 and 0.9265115835486502. The charged_rate of 0.0 throughout describes neutral notation; it does not indicate that the generator lacks ionizable nitrogen.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not systematically vary accessible amine presentation independently of dense scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent ring and side-chain alternatives that vary whether nitrogen is acylated, its accessibility and its distance from aromatic groups while limiting other scaffold changes. The generator should let observed feedback determine where those properties matter, without mandating one amine ring or inferring a required charge state from the submitted strings.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The upper excerpts contain compact aromatic carbonyl systems, whereas the cited saturated replacement of a carbonyl linker scores 0.03343008011310944. Elsewhere an opened carbonyl side-chain analogue scores 0.12467972074136988, and late aryl contraction or carbonyl removal accompanies lower recorded scores within the same visible family. These are local structural associations, not proof that every carbonyl must be retained.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful carbonyl and aromatic arrangements are not consistently preserved during structural diversification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add coherent whole-functional-group and linker replacements that can retain carbonyl orientation and aryl attachment geometry while exploring composition or ring context. Such proposals would test more interpretable chemical alternatives than accumulating disconnected changes to a functional group. Preserve task-agnostic feedback as the criterion for which alternatives prove useful.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
